scenes.title: Born in northwestern Missouri
scenes.assetBrief: Northwestern Missouri prairie and oak woodland, with a modest timber dwelling and split-rail fencing in 1847. The setting represents the Linden area, not a specific property, and the distant figures are not identified as Webbs.

scenes.title: Across the plains at five
scenes.assetBrief: Wide observational charcoal of an organized 1852 ox-wagon company receding across the Nebraska Territory plains beside the Platte corridor. Wagons, loose cattle and distant ambiguous walkers establish scale without identifying Edward or any Webb family member. No handcarts appear, and the descendant recollection of young Edward tending livestock is not converted into a depicted fact.

scenes.title: A father lost beside the Platte
scenes.assetBrief: An 1852 ox-wagon company pauses beside the Platte River at late-summer evening. The landscape establishes the documented setting of Edward Sr.'s death without depicting his illness, death or burial or identifying any figure as a Webb relative.

scenes.title: Coming of age in Utah Territory
scenes.assetBrief: Communal construction at Cove Fort in 1867, with unidentified laborers, unfinished volcanic-stone walls, a timber gate, scaffolding and an ox wagon. Edward is documented at Cove Fort, but no worker shown is identified as him.

scenes.title: Building a life in Arizona Territory
scenes.assetBrief: Public-domain photograph of students at the original dedicated Snowflake Stake Academy building before its destruction by fire in 1910. Edward Milo Webb Jr. opened the academy as its first principal and teacher in 1889, but in a prior log-cabin classroom; this later building represents the institution he helped establish, not his original classroom. Edward is not identified among those pictured.

scenes.title: The line through Sarah Carling
scenes.assetBrief: Sarah Elizabeth Carling Webb with Clark, Jonathan Henry—captioned Henry—Burr, Owen and Catherine in an 1891 A. Miller family photograph.

scenes.title: A date in conflict
scenes.assetBrief: The date 11 September 1921 is strongly supported by the Utah death-certificate index and published Webb family history. One Church History Biographical Database field instead reports 4 April 1924, although the same profile captions Edward 1847–1921. The direct certificate image remains an evidence target.

scenes.title: Missouri to the White Mountains
scenes.assetBrief: Evidence-weighted route graphic on an authentic, rights-cleared 1880 U.S. Geological Survey map. The dashed 1852 line represents the broad Uriah Curtis Company corridor from Missouri through the Platte corridor to the Salt Lake Valley, not an exact daily track. The solid later sequence links documented life places at Salt Lake, Cove Fort, Woodruff and Snowflake without claiming the roads traveled.
scenes.place: Missouri → Platte corridor → Utah → Arizona Territory
